sheets.title: Booklet Challenge · Decimals to Thousandths
sheets.tag: Minia British School · Homework Booklet · U1 L1
sheets.rule: In standard decimal form, every place right of the decimal point must be accounted for. If a place has no value, insert a zero placeholder (0 tenths = .0). "Thousandths" means exactly 3 decimal places.
sheets.question: From Booklet p. 4, Q(3c) & Q(2b): (1) Write in standard form: "6 units, 4 hundredths and 5 thousandths". (2) Write standard form of "4 tenths and 8 thousandths".
steps: Step 1: Identify place values for (1): Units (ones) = 6. Tenths place is omitted, so tenths = 0. Hundredths = 4. Thousandths = 5.
Step 2: Combine places: 6 ones + 0 tenths + 4 hundredths + 5 thousandths = 6.045.
Step 3: Identify place values for (2): Ones = 0. Tenths = 4. Hundredths place is omitted = 0. Thousandths = 8.
Step 4: Combine places: 0.408 (Notice: 0.48 would be 48 hundredths, not thousandths).
sheets.note: Never skip missing place values! When tenths are missing between units and hundredths, always insert a 0 placeholder.

items.label: Question 1 · Booklet p. 4 Q(3c)
items.question: Write in standard form: "6 units, 4 hundredths and 5 thousandths".
steps: Identify place values: Units (ones) = 6. Tenths place is omitted = 0. Hundredths = 4. Thousandths = 5.
Combine places: 6 ones + 0 tenths + 4 hundredths + 5 thousandths = 6.045.

items.label: Question 2 · Booklet p. 4 Q(2b)
items.question: Write standard form of: "4 tenths and 8 thousandths".
steps: Identify place values: Ones = 0. Tenths = 4. Hundredths place is omitted = 0. Thousandths = 8.
Combine places: 0.408 (Notice: 0.48 would be 48 hundredths, not thousandths).

sheets.title: Booklet Challenge · Place Value Shuffle
sheets.tag: Minia British School · Homework Booklet · U1 L2
sheets.rule: To make the greatest decimal less than 10 from given digits, the whole number (ones) part must be the greatest single digit available under 10. Then place remaining digits in descending order after the decimal point.
sheets.question: From Booklet p. 5, Q(3b): Rearrange the digits 3, 5, 1, 8 (with a decimal point) to form the greatest decimal less than 10.
steps: Step 1: Understand the constraint "less than 10": The number can only have a single whole number digit (ones place), because two whole digits would be ≥ 10.
Step 2: Pick the greatest available digit for the ones place: The digits are {1, 3, 5, 8}. The greatest is 8, so ones = 8 (giving 8.xxx < 10).
Step 3: Arrange remaining digits {5, 3, 1} descending to maximize value: Tenths = 5, Hundredths = 3, Thousandths = 1.
Step 4: Verify: 8.531 is less than 10 and greater than all other combinations (8.513, 8.351, 8.315, etc.).
sheets.note: The ones place has the largest impact on value. Setting 8 as the whole number ensures the maximum decimal value under 10.

sheets.title: Booklet Challenge · Composing & Decomposing
sheets.tag: Minia British School · Homework Booklet · U1 L3
sheets.rule: A decimal is decomposed into Expanded Form by writing the sum of the values of each non-zero digit. Zero digits indicate empty places and are omitted in standard expanded addition.
sheets.question: From Booklet p. 6, Q(3a) & Q(2a): (1) Decompose 12.408 into expanded form and word units. (2) Identify the sum equivalent to 4.503.
steps: Step 1: Determine the value of each digit in 12.408: 1 ten = 10, 2 ones = 2, 4 tenths = 0.4, 0 hundredths (omitted), 8 thousandths = 0.008.
Step 2: Write Expanded Form: 12.408 = 10 + 2 + 0.4 + 0.008.
Step 3: Write Unit Form: 1 ten, 2 ones, 4 tenths, 8 thousandths (or 12 ones and 408 thousandths).
Step 4: Check 4.503: 4 ones + 5 tenths (0.5) + 3 thousandths (0.003) = 4 + 0.5 + 0.003.
sheets.note: Distinguish 0.008 from 0.08! Thousandths have two zeros between the decimal point and the digit when tenths and hundredths are zero.

items.label: Question 1 · Booklet p. 6 Q(3a)
items.question: Decompose 12.408 into expanded form and word units.
steps: Determine digit values: 1 ten = 10, 2 ones = 2, 4 tenths = 0.4, 0 hundredths, 8 thousandths = 0.008.
Unit Form: 1 ten, 2 ones, 4 tenths, 8 thousandths.

items.label: Question 2 · Booklet p. 6 Q(2a)
items.question: Identify the sum equivalent to 4.503.
steps: Break down 4.503: 4 ones (4) + 5 tenths (0.5) + 3 thousandths (0.003).
Combine parts: 4 + 0.5 + 0.003.

sheets.title: Booklet Challenge · Comparing Decimals
sheets.tag: Minia British School · Homework Booklet · U1 L4
sheets.rule: To compare or order decimals with different numbers of decimal digits, pad shorter decimals with trailing zeros until all numbers have equal decimal places (thousandths).
sheets.question: From Booklet p. 7, Q(3a) & Q(3b): (1) Order from least to greatest: 2.45 , 2.4 , 2.405 , 2.54. (2) Order from greatest to least: 0.7 , 0.07 , 0.77 , 0.707.
steps: Step 1: Equalize places for set (1) to thousandths: 2.450 , 2.400 , 2.405 , 2.540.
Step 2: Compare decimal parts: 400 < 405 < 450 < 540. Order: 2.4 < 2.405 < 2.45 < 2.54.
Step 3: Equalize places for set (2) to thousandths: 0.700 , 0.070 , 0.770 , 0.707.
Step 4: Compare from greatest to least: 770 > 707 > 700 > 70. Order: 0.77 > 0.707 > 0.7 > 0.07.
sheets.note: More digits does not mean greater value! 2.405 has 4 digits but is smaller than 2.45 (2.450). Always pad zeros first.

items.question: Order from least to greatest: 2.45 , 2.4 , 2.405 , 2.54.
steps: Equalize places to thousandths: 2.450 , 2.400 , 2.405 , 2.540.
Compare decimal parts: 400 < 405 < 450 < 540.
Ascending order: 2.4 < 2.405 < 2.45 < 2.54.

items.question: Order from greatest to least: 0.7 , 0.07 , 0.77 , 0.707.

sheets.title: Booklet Challenge · Rounding Decimals
sheets.tag: Minia British School · Homework Booklet · U1 L5
sheets.rule: When rounding to the nearest hundredth, inspect the thousandths digit. If the rounding place is 9 and we round up, the carry cascades to tenths and ones places.
sheets.question: From Booklet p. 8, Q(3a) & Q(3b): (1) Round 0.999 to the nearest hundredth. (2) Round 11.98 to the nearest tenth.
steps: Step 1: For 0.999 to hundredths: Underline hundredths: 0.99[9]. Look at thousandths digit (9).
Step 2: Since 9 ≥ 5, round up: 9 hundredths + 1 = 10 (write 0, carry 1 to tenths) → 9 tenths + 1 = 10 (write 0, carry 1 to ones) → 0 + 1 = 1.
Step 3: Result: 1.00 (Must keep two decimal zeros to show hundredths precision!).
Step 4: For 11.98 to tenths: Underline tenths: 11.9[8]. Hundredths digit is 8 ≥ 5 → round up: 9 + 1 = 10 tenths → 12.0.
sheets.note: Keep the trailing zeros! Writing 1 instead of 1.00 loses the specified hundredths precision required on exams.

items.label: Question 1 · Booklet p. 8 Q(3a)
items.question: Round 0.999 to the nearest hundredth.
steps: Underline hundredths digit: 0.99[9]. Look at thousandths digit (9).
9 ≥ 5 → round up: 9 hundredths + 1 = 10 (carry 1 to tenths) → 9 + 1 = 10 (carry 1 to ones) → 1.00.
Keep two decimal zeros to show hundredths precision.

items.label: Question 2 · Booklet p. 8 Q(3b)
items.question: Round 11.98 to the nearest tenth.
steps: Underline tenths digit: 11.9[8]. Hundredths digit is 8 ≥ 5.
Round up: 9 tenths + 1 = 10 tenths → carry 1 to ones: 11 + 1 = 12.0.

sheets.title: Booklet Challenge · Estimating Sums
sheets.tag: Minia British School · Homework Booklet · U1 L6
sheets.rule: To estimate decimal sums, rounding to the nearest whole number gives a very practical and accurate benchmark for everyday money and measurements.
sheets.question: From Booklet p. 9, Q(3b) & Q(4a): (1) Estimate then add: 12.34 + 7.85. (2) Ahmed bought a book for 18.75 L.E and a pen for 6.30 L.E. Estimate the total cost.
steps: Step 1: Estimate 12.34 + 7.85 by rounding to nearest whole: 12.34 rounds to 12; 7.85 rounds to 8. Estimate: 12 + 8 = 20.
Step 2: Calculate actual sum: 12.34 + 7.85 = 20.19. The estimate 20 is close and reasonable (diff = 0.19).
Step 3: Estimate Ahmed purchases: 18.75 L.E rounds to 19 L.E; 6.30 L.E rounds to 6 L.E.
Step 4: Estimated total: 19 + 6 = 25 L.E (Actual total = 18.75 + 6.30 = 25.05 L.E; diff = only 0.05 L.E!).
sheets.note: Always compare your estimate with the exact sum to confirm that your calculated answer makes sense.

items.question: Estimate then add: 12.34 + 7.85.
steps: Round to nearest whole: 12.34 rounds to 12; 7.85 rounds to 8.
Estimate: 12 + 8 = 20. Actual: 12.34 + 7.85 = 20.19 (Reasonable, diff = 0.19).

items.label: Question 2 · Booklet p. 9 Q(4a)
items.question: Ahmed bought a book for 18.75 L.E and a pen for 6.30 L.E. Estimate the total cost.
steps: Round purchases: 18.75 L.E rounds to 19 L.E; 6.30 L.E rounds to 6 L.E.
Estimated total: 19 + 6 = 25 L.E. (Actual: 18.75 + 6.30 = 25.05 L.E, diff = 0.05 L.E).

sheets.title: Booklet Challenge · Adding Decimals
sheets.tag: Minia British School · Homework Booklet · U1 L7
sheets.rule: To add three decimals with varying lengths, align every decimal point vertically, pad missing places with zeros, and add from right to left with regrouping.
sheets.question: From Booklet p. 10, Q(3b) & Q(2a): (1) Find: 12.4 + 6.35 + 0.08. (2) Calculate 14.56 + 9.89.
steps: Step 1: Align vertically and pad 12.4 to 12.40: 12.40 + 6.35 + 0.08.
Step 2: Add hundredths column: 0 + 5 + 8 = 13 hundredths → write 3, carry 1 to tenths.
Step 3: Add tenths column: 1 (carried) + 4 + 3 + 0 = 8 tenths.
Step 4: Add whole numbers: 12 + 6 + 0 = 18 ones → Result = 18.83.
sheets.note: Pad 12.4 with a zero so it becomes 12.40. Misaligning tenths with hundredths is the most frequent calculation error.

items.label: Question 1 · Booklet p. 10 Q(3b)
items.question: Find: 12.4 + 6.35 + 0.08.
steps: Hundredths: 0 + 5 + 8 = 13 (write 3, carry 1). Tenths: 1 + 4 + 3 + 0 = 8. Ones: 12 + 6 = 18.

items.label: Question 2 · Booklet p. 10 Q(2a)
items.question: Calculate: 14.56 + 9.89.
steps: Align vertically: 14.56 + 9.89.
Hundredths: 6 + 9 = 15 (5, carry 1). Tenths: 1 + 5 + 8 = 14 (4, carry 1). Ones: 1 + 14 + 9 = 24.

sheets.title: Booklet Challenge · Modeling Subtraction
sheets.tag: Minia British School · Homework Booklet · U1 L8
sheets.rule: When subtracting a decimal from a whole number, rewrite the whole number with a decimal point and zeros (12 = 12.00, 1 = 1.000). Regroup across zeros from left to right.
sheets.question: From Booklet p. 11, Q(3b) & Q(2b): (1) Find: 12 − 5.47. (2) Calculate: 1 − 0.001.
steps: Step 1: Rewrite 12 as 12.00 to match the 2 decimal places of 5.47.
Step 2: Regroup from ones across tenths into hundredths: 12.00 becomes 11 ones, 9 tenths, and 10 hundredths.
Step 3: Subtract: 10 − 7 = 3 (hundredths); 9 − 4 = 5 (tenths); 11 − 5 = 6 (ones) → 6.53.
Step 4: For (2): 1.000 − 0.001: 1 one regrouped gives 9 tenths, 9 hundredths, 10 thousandths. 10 − 1 = 9 → 0.999.
sheets.note: Check by adding back: 6.53 + 5.47 = 12.00 and 0.999 + 0.001 = 1.000. Inverse addition verifies subtraction instantly.

items.label: Question 1 · Booklet p. 11 Q(3b)
items.question: Find: 12 − 5.47.
steps: Rewrite 12 as 12.00 to match decimal places of 5.47.
Regroup: 12.00 becomes 11 ones, 9 tenths, 10 hundredths.
Subtract: 10 − 7 = 3 (hundredths); 9 − 4 = 5 (tenths); 11 − 5 = 6 (ones) → 6.53.

items.label: Question 2 · Booklet p. 11 Q(2b)
items.question: Calculate: 1 − 0.001.
steps: Rewrite 1 as 1.000 to match thousandths.
Regroup 1 one into 9 tenths, 9 hundredths, 10 thousandths.
Subtract: 10 − 1 = 9 (thousandths); 9 − 0 = 9; 9 − 0 = 9 → 0.999.

sheets.title: Booklet Challenge · Estimating Differences
sheets.tag: Minia British School · Homework Booklet · U1 L9
sheets.rule: To estimate decimal differences, round each number to the nearest whole before subtracting. Compare with the exact difference to verify reasonability.
sheets.question: From Booklet p. 12, Q(3b) & Q(4a): (1) Estimate then subtract: 24.35 − 11.68. (2) A shopper had 50 L.E and spent 27.65 L.E. Estimate the change and calculate actual.
steps: Step 1: Estimate 24.35 − 11.68: 24.35 rounds to 24; 11.68 rounds to 12. Estimated difference: 24 − 12 = 12.
Step 2: Calculate actual difference: 24.35 − 11.68 = 12.67 (Difference between estimate and actual is only 0.67).
Step 3: Estimate shopper change: 50 − 28 = 22 L.E (rounding 27.65 to 28).
Step 4: Calculate exact change: 50.00 − 27.65 = 22.35 L.E (Estimate 22 L.E is within 0.35 L.E).
sheets.note: Because 27.65 is closer to 28 than 27, rounding up to 28 gives an estimate of 22, very close to the exact 22.35 L.E.

items.label: Question 1 · Booklet p. 12 Q(3b)
items.question: Estimate then subtract: 24.35 − 11.68.
steps: Round to whole: 24.35 → 24; 11.68 → 12. Estimated difference: 24 − 12 = 12.
Calculate actual difference: 24.35 − 11.68 = 12.67 (Difference = 0.67).

items.label: Question 2 · Booklet p. 12 Q(4a)
items.question: A shopper had 50 L.E and spent 27.65 L.E. Estimate the change and calculate actual.
steps: Estimate: 50 − 28 = 22 L.E (rounding 27.65 to 28).
Actual change: 50.00 − 27.65 = 22.35 L.E (Estimate 22 L.E is within 0.35 L.E).

sheets.title: Booklet Challenge · Subtracting to Thousandths
sheets.tag: Minia British School · Homework Booklet · U1 L10
sheets.rule: Subtracting across three decimal zeros requires cascade regrouping from the whole number through tenths and hundredths into thousandths.
sheets.question: From Booklet p. 13, Q(3b) & Q(4a): (1) Find: 20 − 13.256. (2) A wire was 4.5 m long. A piece of 1.275 m was cut. How long is the remaining wire?
steps: Step 2: Regroup from 20 ones → leaves 19 ones, 9 tenths, 9 hundredths, and 10 thousandths.
Step 3: Subtract: 10 − 6 = 4 (thous.); 9 − 5 = 4 (hund.); 9 − 2 = 7 (tenths); 19 − 13 = 6 (ones) → 6.744.
sheets.note: Remember to pad 4.5 m with two zeros to make 4.500 m before subtracting 1.275 m!

items.question: Find: 20 − 13.256.
steps: Regroup 20 ones → leaves 19 ones, 9 tenths, 9 hundredths, 10 thousandths.

items.label: Question 2 · Booklet p. 13 Q(4a)
items.question: A wire was 4.5 m long. A piece of 1.275 m was cut. How long is the remaining wire?
steps: Pad to thousandths: 4.500 − 1.275.
Regroup: 4.500 becomes 4.4(9)(10).

sheets.title: Booklet Challenge · Decimal Story Problems
sheets.tag: Minia British School · Homework Booklet · U1 L11
sheets.rule: Multi-step story problems require identifying intermediate totals first (addition) before finding the final unknown (subtraction).
sheets.question: From Booklet p. 14, Q(4a) & Q(1a): (1) Sara bought a bag for 145.75 L.E and shoes for 89.5 L.E. She paid with 300 L.E. How much change did she receive? (2) If a + 3.45 = 7.2, find a.
steps: Step 1: Step 1 (Total spent): Add bag and shoes: 145.75 + 89.50 = 235.25 L.E.
Step 2: Step 2 (Change received): Subtract total spent from 300 L.E: 300.00 − 235.25.
Step 3: Regroup 300.00: 300 becomes 299 and 100 hundredths. 300.00 − 235.25 = 64.75 L.E.
sheets.answer: (1) Total spent = 235.25 L.E | Change = 64.75 L.E  |  (2) a = 3.75
sheets.note: Break word problems into clearly labeled steps: Step 1 = Total purchases, Step 2 = Change. Check: 235.25 + 64.75 = 300.00 L.E.

items.question: Sara bought a bag for 145.75 L.E and shoes for 89.5 L.E. She paid with 300 L.E. How much change did she receive?
steps: Step 1 (Total spent): Add purchases: 145.75 + 89.50 = 235.25 L.E.
Step 2 (Change received): Subtract total from 300: 300.00 − 235.25 = 64.75 L.E.

items.question: If a + 3.45 = 7.2, find the value of a.
steps: Use inverse operation: a = 7.20 − 3.45.

sheets.title: Booklet Challenge · Expressions vs Equations
sheets.tag: Minia British School · Homework Booklet · U2 L1
sheets.rule: An Expression has no equals sign (e.g. x − 5.23). An Equation equates two expressions with "=" (e.g. x − 5.23 = 9.42). In "subtract A from B", B comes FIRST: B − A.
sheets.question: From Booklet p. 15, Q(2b) & Q(1): (1) Write an equation: "We subtract 5.23 from a number to get a result of 9.42". (2) Distinguish: Which of m + 6 = 9, 1.2 − m = 0.2, m + 44 is an expression?
steps: Step 1: Analyze English phrasing "subtract 5.23 from a number": Let the unknown number be x. Subtracting 5.23 from x means x is the starting amount (minuend).
Step 2: Formulate the equation: x − 5.23 = 9.42. (Common error: writing 5.23 − x = 9.42 which is incorrect!).
Step 3: For part (2): Look for the presence of an equals sign "=".
Step 4: m + 6 = 9 (equation), 1.2 − m = 0.2 (equation). Only "m + 44" has no equals sign, so it is an algebraic expression.
sheets.answer: (1) Equation: x − 5.23 = 9.42  |  (2) Expression: m + 44 (Equations: m + 6 = 9, 1.2 − m = 0.2)
sheets.note: Remember the phrase "subtract from": the number following "from" is always written first in the subtraction expression!

items.label: Question 1 · Booklet p. 15 Q(2b)
items.question: Write an equation: "We subtract 5.23 from a number to get a result of 9.42".
steps: Let unknown number be x. Subtracting 5.23 from x means x is the minuend.
Write equation: x − 5.23 = 9.42 (Caution: 5.23 − x is incorrect).

items.label: Question 2 · Booklet p. 15 Q(1)
items.question: Distinguish: Which of m + 6 = 9, 1.2 − m = 0.2, m + 44 is an expression?
steps: Look for an equals sign '='.
m + 6 = 9 and 1.2 − m = 0.2 have '=' so they are equations.
m + 44 has no equals sign, so it is an algebraic expression.
items.answer: Expression: m + 44  (m + 6 = 9 and 1.2 − m = 0.2 are equations)

sheets.title: Booklet Challenge · Variables in Equations
sheets.tag: Minia British School · Homework Booklet · U2 L2
sheets.rule: When solving subtraction equations: If variable is minuend (A − b = c), add: A = c + b. If variable is subtrahend (a − z = c), subtract: z = a − c.
sheets.question: From Booklet p. 16, Q(3a) & Q(3b): Solve for the variable: (1) A − 32.61 = 12.28  |  (2) 3.245 − z = 1.265.
steps: Step 1: Analyze (1) A − 32.61 = 12.28: A is the total (whole). To find the whole, add the parts: A = 12.28 + 32.61.
Step 3: Analyze (2) 3.245 − z = 1.265: 3.245 is the whole; z and 1.265 are the parts. To find the missing part z, subtract: z = 3.245 − 1.265.
sheets.note: Use a Bar Model to check! In A − 32.61 = 12.28, A sits at the top (whole). In 3.245 − z = 1.265, 3.245 sits at the top, so z = 3.245 − 1.265.

items.question: Solve for the variable: A − 32.61 = 12.28.
steps: A is the total (whole). Add the parts: A = 12.28 + 32.61.

items.label: Question 2 · Booklet p. 16 Q(3b)
items.question: Solve for the variable: 3.245 − z = 1.265.
steps: 3.245 is the whole; z is a missing part. Subtract: z = 3.245 − 1.265.

sheets.title: Booklet Challenge · Stories with Numbers
sheets.tag: Minia British School · Homework Booklet · U2 L3
sheets.rule: "less than" reverses word order: "5 less than x" means x − 5 (NOT 5 − x). In age word problems, set up an equation with a variable before solving.
sheets.question: From Booklet p. 17, Q(2a), Q(3b) & Q(4a): (1) Write expression: "5 less than x". (2) Write & solve: "When 7 is subtracted from a number, the result is 15". (3) Mona is 3 years older than brother. If Mona is 12, how old is her brother?
steps: Step 1: For (1): "5 less than x" translates to x − 5.
Step 2: For (2): Let the number be n. "7 is subtracted from n" gives n − 7. "Result is 15" gives equation: n − 7 = 15. Solve: n = 15 + 7 = 22.
Step 3: For (3): Let brother age be b. Mona is 3 years older → b + 3 = 12 (or 12 − b = 3).
Step 4: Solve for brother age: b = 12 − 3 = 9 years old.
sheets.answer: (1) x − 5  |  (2) Equation: n − 7 = 15 ⇒ n = 22  |  (3) Equation: b + 3 = 12 ⇒ Brother is 9 years old
sheets.note: Beware the "less than" trap: 5 less than 10 is 10 − 5 = 5, not 5 − 10. So "5 less than x" is ALWAYS x − 5.

items.label: Question 1 · Booklet p. 17 Q(2a)
items.question: Write expression: "5 less than x".
steps: "5 less than x" means subtracting 5 from x.
Expression: x − 5.

items.label: Question 2 · Booklet p. 17 Q(3b)

assessmentSheets.title: October Assessment · Multiply decimal by 10

steps: Start with 4.56.

assessmentSheets.note: Moving the point right increases the value.

assessmentSheets.title: October Assessment · Value change of a digit
assessmentSheets.rule: When a number is multiplied by 10, every digit shifts one place to the left, and its value increases by 10 times.
assessmentSheets.question:
Choose: If the decimal number 7.23 is multiplied by 10, then the value of the digit 2 will be ......
(a) 20   (b) 2   (c) 0.2   (d) 0.02
steps: In 7.23, the digit 2 is in the tenths place, so its original value is 0.2.
When multiplied by 10: 7.23 × 10 = 72.3.
In 72.3, the digit 2 is now in the ones place.
The value of 2 in the ones place is 2 (0.2 × 10 = 2).
assessmentSheets.note: Tenths × 10 becomes ones.

- Ones: 5 + 9 + 1 = 15 (5, carry 1)
- Tens: 2 + 1 + 1 = 4 → Total = 45.00 = 45 pounds.

2) Total money = 45 pounds

1) Huda bought a silver ring of mass 3.245 grams, and Mona bought a chain of mass 5.318 grams. Calculate the difference between the two masses, then find the actual difference.
2) A road is 35.347 km long, and the train has covered 22.192 km. Calculate the remaining distance.
steps:
Problem 1:
- Estimated difference (nearest whole): 5 − 3 = 2 grams.
- Actual difference: 5.318 − 3.245 = 2.073 grams.
  (8−5=3; 11−4=7; 2−2=0; 5−3=2 → 2.073 g).

Problem 2:
- Remaining distance = 35.347 − 22.192.
- Thousandths: 7 − 2 = 5.
- Hundredths: 4 < 9, borrow: 14 − 9 = 5.
- Tenths: 2 − 1 = 1.
- Ones: 5 − 2 = 3. Tens: 3 − 2 = 1 → 13.155 km.
assessmentSheets.answer:
1) Estimated diff ≈ 2 g ; Actual diff = 2.073 grams
2) Remaining distance = 13.155 kilometers
assessmentSheets.note: Check remaining + covered: 13.155 + 22.192 = 35.347 km.

assessmentSheets.title: October Assessment · Identify Equations vs Expressions
assessmentSheets.rule: An equation must have an equal sign (=). An expression has numbers, operations, or variables but NO equal sign.
assessmentSheets.question:
Which of the following represents an equation?
a) x + 2.4 = y
b) 2x + 8
steps: Option a: 'x + 2.4 = y' contains an equal sign (=) showing two equal sides.
Option b: '2x + 8' has an addition operation and a variable, but no equal sign.
Since an equation is defined as a mathematical statement containing an equal sign (=), option a is the equation.
assessmentSheets.answer: a) x + 2.4 = y is an equation (b is a mathematical expression)
assessmentSheets.note: Look for '=': equal sign present = equation; no '=' = expression.

assessmentSheets.title: October Assessment · Solve Equations & Bar Model
assessmentSheets.rule: In a bar model: Whole = Part + Part. When the whole is unknown, add parts. When a part is unknown, subtract from the whole.
assessmentSheets.question:
1) Find the value of A in the equation: 5.402 − A = 2.230
2) Find the unknown using the bar model:
a) D − 2.405 = 3.712
b) 5.391 + N = 8.207
steps:
Problem 2a: D − 2.405 = 3.712.
D is the Whole (top of bar model). Parts are 2.405 and 3.712.
D = 2.405 + 3.712 = 6.117.

Problem 2b: 5.391 + N = 8.207.
8.207 is the Whole (top of bar model). Parts are 5.391 and N.
N = 8.207 − 5.391 = 2.816.
assessmentSheets.note: In subtraction (Whole − Part = Part), the first number is always the Whole.

items.label: Problem 1 · Subtraction Equation
items.question: Find the value of A in the equation: 5.402 − A = 2.230.
steps: 5.402 is the Whole, A is a missing Part: A = 5.402 − 2.230.

items.label: Problem 2 · Bar Model Equations
items.question:
Find the unknown using the bar model:
(a) D − 2.405 = 3.712
(b) 5.391 + N = 8.207
steps: (a) D is the Whole (top): D = 2.405 + 3.712 = 6.117.

assessmentSheets.title: October Assessment · Write Equations & Meaning of Variable
assessmentSheets.rule: Use a letter (variable) for the unknown amount and write the relationship as an equation.
assessmentSheets.question:
1) Write the equation that represents: The sum of two numbers is 28.73. If the first number is 15.06, what is the other number?
2) Mohamad caught a fish of mass 1.367 kg, and another fish of mass 1.529 kg. Mohamad wrote: X = 1.367 + 1.529. Write what X represents.
steps:
Problem 1: Let the unknown number be x (or n).
The sum is 28.73, so: 15.06 + x = 28.73 (or x = 28.73 − 15.06).
Solving gives: x = 28.73 − 15.06 = 13.67.

Problem 2: Look at the equation X = 1.367 + 1.529.
1.367 kg is the mass of the first fish, and 1.529 kg is the mass of the second fish.
Adding them gives the total mass of both fish.
Therefore, X represents the total mass of the two fish in kilograms.
assessmentSheets.answer:
1) Equation: 15.06 + x = 28.73 (other number = 13.67)
2) X represents the total mass of the two fish in kilograms
assessmentSheets.note: A variable represents an unknown quantity described in the story.

items.question: Write the equation: The sum of two numbers is 28.73. If the first number is 15.06, what is the other number?
steps: Let unknown number be x. Equation: 15.06 + x = 28.73.

items.label: Problem 2 · Variable Meaning
items.question: Mohamad caught fish of 1.367 kg and 1.529 kg. He wrote: X = 1.367 + 1.529. What does X represent?
steps: 1.367 kg is first fish; 1.529 kg is second fish.
Adding them gives the total combined mass.
X represents the total mass of the two fish in kilograms.
items.answer: X represents total mass of the two fish in kilograms

assessmentSheets.title: October Assessment · Common Multiples & Prime Numbers
assessmentSheets.rule: A common multiple of two numbers is divisible by both. A prime number has only two factors: 1 and itself.
assessmentSheets.question:
1) Choose: The number 40 is a common multiple for the two numbers ......
(a) 4, 7   (b) 6, 5   (c) 8, 4   (d) 4, 6

2) Find the smallest odd prime number.
steps:
Problem 1: Test the pairs for dividing into 40:
- 40 is divisible by 4 (4 × 10 = 40) and by 8 (8 × 5 = 40).
- 40 is not divisible by 7 or 6.
- Thus, 40 is a common multiple of 8 and 4.

Problem 2: Prime numbers are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, ...
- 2 is the smallest prime number, but 2 is EVEN.
- The next prime number is 3, which is ODD.
- Therefore, the smallest odd prime number is 3.
assessmentSheets.note: 2 is the ONLY even prime number; 3 is the smallest odd prime.

assessmentSheets.title: October Assessment · Prime Factors & Greatest Common Factor (GCF)
assessmentSheets.rule: To find a number from its prime factors, multiply them. GCF is the product of common prime factors.
assessmentSheets.question:
1) What is the number whose prime factors are 2, 3 and 3?
2) Two numbers, the prime factors of the first are (2, 2, 3) and the second are (2, 3, 3). Find their Greatest Common Factor (GCF).
steps:
Problem 1: Multiply the prime factors:
Number = 2 × 3 × 3 = 6 × 3 = 18.

Problem 2: Find common prime factors between (2, 2, 3) and (2, 3, 3):
- Common factor 1: both have one 2.
- Common factor 2: both have one 3.
- Product of common prime factors = 2 × 3 = 6.
- Therefore, GCF = 6.
assessmentSheets.note: First number is 12, second number is 18; their common factors are 1, 2, 3, 6.

steps: Identify common prime factors: one 2 and one 3.

assessmentSheets.title: Booklet Challenge · Decimals to Thousandths
assessmentSheets.tag: Minia British School · Homework Booklet · U1 L1
assessmentSheets.rule: In standard decimal form, every place right of the decimal point must be accounted for. If a place has no value, insert a zero placeholder (0 tenths = .0). "Thousandths" means exactly 3 decimal places.
assessmentSheets.question: From Booklet p. 4, Q(3c) & Q(2b): (1) Write in standard form: "6 units, 4 hundredths and 5 thousandths". (2) Write standard form of "4 tenths and 8 thousandths".
steps: Step 1: Identify place values for (1): Units (ones) = 6. Tenths place is omitted, so tenths = 0. Hundredths = 4. Thousandths = 5.
Step 2: Combine places: 6 ones + 0 tenths + 4 hundredths + 5 thousandths = 6.045.
Step 3: Identify place values for (2): Ones = 0. Tenths = 4. Hundredths place is omitted = 0. Thousandths = 8.
Step 4: Combine places: 0.408 (Notice: 0.48 would be 48 hundredths, not thousandths).
assessmentSheets.note: Never skip missing place values! When tenths are missing between units and hundredths, always insert a 0 placeholder.

items.label: Question 1 · Booklet p. 4 Q(3c)
items.question: Write in standard form: "6 units, 4 hundredths and 5 thousandths".
steps: Identify place values: Units (ones) = 6. Tenths place is omitted = 0. Hundredths = 4. Thousandths = 5.
Combine places: 6 ones + 0 tenths + 4 hundredths + 5 thousandths = 6.045.

items.label: Question 2 · Booklet p. 4 Q(2b)
items.question: Write standard form of: "4 tenths and 8 thousandths".
steps: Identify place values: Ones = 0. Tenths = 4. Hundredths place is omitted = 0. Thousandths = 8.
Combine places: 0.408 (Notice: 0.48 would be 48 hundredths, not thousandths).

assessmentSheets.title: Booklet Challenge · Place Value Shuffle
assessmentSheets.tag: Minia British School · Homework Booklet · U1 L2
assessmentSheets.rule: To make the greatest decimal less than 10 from given digits, the whole number (ones) part must be the greatest single digit available under 10. Then place remaining digits in descending order after the decimal point.
assessmentSheets.question: From Booklet p. 5, Q(3b): Rearrange the digits 3, 5, 1, 8 (with a decimal point) to form the greatest decimal less than 10.
steps: Step 1: Understand the constraint "less than 10": The number can only have a single whole number digit (ones place), because two whole digits would be ≥ 10.
Step 2: Pick the greatest available digit for the ones place: The digits are {1, 3, 5, 8}. The greatest is 8, so ones = 8 (giving 8.xxx < 10).
Step 3: Arrange remaining digits {5, 3, 1} descending to maximize value: Tenths = 5, Hundredths = 3, Thousandths = 1.
Step 4: Verify: 8.531 is less than 10 and greater than all other combinations (8.513, 8.351, 8.315, etc.).
assessmentSheets.note: The ones place has the largest impact on value. Setting 8 as the whole number ensures the maximum decimal value under 10.

assessmentSheets.title: Booklet Challenge · Composing & Decomposing
assessmentSheets.tag: Minia British School · Homework Booklet · U1 L3
assessmentSheets.rule: A decimal is decomposed into Expanded Form by writing the sum of the values of each non-zero digit. Zero digits indicate empty places and are omitted in standard expanded addition.
assessmentSheets.question: From Booklet p. 6, Q(3a) & Q(2a): (1) Decompose 12.408 into expanded form and word units. (2) Identify the sum equivalent to 4.503.
steps: Step 1: Determine the value of each digit in 12.408: 1 ten = 10, 2 ones = 2, 4 tenths = 0.4, 0 hundredths (omitted), 8 thousandths = 0.008.
Step 2: Write Expanded Form: 12.408 = 10 + 2 + 0.4 + 0.008.
Step 3: Write Unit Form: 1 ten, 2 ones, 4 tenths, 8 thousandths (or 12 ones and 408 thousandths).
Step 4: Check 4.503: 4 ones + 5 tenths (0.5) + 3 thousandths (0.003) = 4 + 0.5 + 0.003.
assessmentSheets.note: Distinguish 0.008 from 0.08! Thousandths have two zeros between the decimal point and the digit when tenths and hundredths are zero.

items.label: Question 1 · Booklet p. 6 Q(3a)
items.question: Decompose 12.408 into expanded form and word units.
steps: Determine digit values: 1 ten = 10, 2 ones = 2, 4 tenths = 0.4, 0 hundredths, 8 thousandths = 0.008.
Unit Form: 1 ten, 2 ones, 4 tenths, 8 thousandths.

items.question: Identify the sum equivalent to 4.503.
steps: Break down 4.503: 4 ones (4) + 5 tenths (0.5) + 3 thousandths (0.003).
Combine parts: 4 + 0.5 + 0.003.

assessmentSheets.title: Booklet Challenge · Comparing Decimals
assessmentSheets.tag: Minia British School · Homework Booklet · U1 L4
assessmentSheets.rule: To compare or order decimals with different numbers of decimal digits, pad shorter decimals with trailing zeros until all numbers have equal decimal places (thousandths).
assessmentSheets.question: From Booklet p. 7, Q(3a) & Q(3b): (1) Order from least to greatest: 2.45 , 2.4 , 2.405 , 2.54. (2) Order from greatest to least: 0.7 , 0.07 , 0.77 , 0.707.
steps: Step 1: Equalize places for set (1) to thousandths: 2.450 , 2.400 , 2.405 , 2.540.
Step 2: Compare decimal parts: 400 < 405 < 450 < 540. Order: 2.4 < 2.405 < 2.45 < 2.54.
Step 3: Equalize places for set (2) to thousandths: 0.700 , 0.070 , 0.770 , 0.707.
Step 4: Compare from greatest to least: 770 > 707 > 700 > 70. Order: 0.77 > 0.707 > 0.7 > 0.07.
assessmentSheets.note: More digits does not mean greater value! 2.405 has 4 digits but is smaller than 2.45 (2.450). Always pad zeros first.

items.question: Order from least to greatest: 2.45 , 2.4 , 2.405 , 2.54.
steps: Equalize places to thousandths: 2.450 , 2.400 , 2.405 , 2.540.
Compare decimal parts: 400 < 405 < 450 < 540.
Ascending order: 2.4 < 2.405 < 2.45 < 2.54.

items.label: Question 2 · Booklet p. 7 Q(3b)
items.question: Order from greatest to least: 0.7 , 0.07 , 0.77 , 0.707.

assessmentSheets.title: Booklet Challenge · Rounding Decimals
assessmentSheets.tag: Minia British School · Homework Booklet · U1 L5
assessmentSheets.rule: When rounding to the nearest hundredth, inspect the thousandths digit. If the rounding place is 9 and we round up, the carry cascades to tenths and ones places.
assessmentSheets.question: From Booklet p. 8, Q(3a) & Q(3b): (1) Round 0.999 to the nearest hundredth. (2) Round 11.98 to the nearest tenth.
steps: Step 1: For 0.999 to hundredths: Underline hundredths: 0.99[9]. Look at thousandths digit (9).
Step 2: Since 9 ≥ 5, round up: 9 hundredths + 1 = 10 (write 0, carry 1 to tenths) → 9 tenths + 1 = 10 (write 0, carry 1 to ones) → 0 + 1 = 1.
Step 3: Result: 1.00 (Must keep two decimal zeros to show hundredths precision!).
Step 4: For 11.98 to tenths: Underline tenths: 11.9[8]. Hundredths digit is 8 ≥ 5 → round up: 9 + 1 = 10 tenths → 12.0.
assessmentSheets.note: Keep the trailing zeros! Writing 1 instead of 1.00 loses the specified hundredths precision required on exams.

items.label: Question 1 · Booklet p. 8 Q(3a)
items.question: Round 0.999 to the nearest hundredth.
steps: Underline hundredths digit: 0.99[9]. Look at thousandths digit (9).
9 ≥ 5 → round up: 9 hundredths + 1 = 10 (carry 1 to tenths) → 9 + 1 = 10 (carry 1 to ones) → 1.00.
Keep two decimal zeros to show hundredths precision.

items.label: Question 2 · Booklet p. 8 Q(3b)
items.question: Round 11.98 to the nearest tenth.
steps: Underline tenths digit: 11.9[8]. Hundredths digit is 8 ≥ 5.
Round up: 9 tenths + 1 = 10 tenths → carry 1 to ones: 11 + 1 = 12.0.

assessmentSheets.title: Booklet Challenge · Estimating Sums
assessmentSheets.tag: Minia British School · Homework Booklet · U1 L6
assessmentSheets.rule: To estimate decimal sums, rounding to the nearest whole number gives a very practical and accurate benchmark for everyday money and measurements.
assessmentSheets.question: From Booklet p. 9, Q(3b) & Q(4a): (1) Estimate then add: 12.34 + 7.85. (2) Ahmed bought a book for 18.75 L.E and a pen for 6.30 L.E. Estimate the total cost.
steps: Step 1: Estimate 12.34 + 7.85 by rounding to nearest whole: 12.34 rounds to 12; 7.85 rounds to 8. Estimate: 12 + 8 = 20.
Step 2: Calculate actual sum: 12.34 + 7.85 = 20.19. The estimate 20 is close and reasonable (diff = 0.19).
Step 3: Estimate Ahmed purchases: 18.75 L.E rounds to 19 L.E; 6.30 L.E rounds to 6 L.E.
Step 4: Estimated total: 19 + 6 = 25 L.E (Actual total = 18.75 + 6.30 = 25.05 L.E; diff = only 0.05 L.E!).
assessmentSheets.note: Always compare your estimate with the exact sum to confirm that your calculated answer makes sense.

items.label: Question 1 · Booklet p. 9 Q(3b)
items.question: Estimate then add: 12.34 + 7.85.
steps: Round to nearest whole: 12.34 rounds to 12; 7.85 rounds to 8.
Estimate: 12 + 8 = 20. Actual: 12.34 + 7.85 = 20.19 (Reasonable, diff = 0.19).

items.label: Question 2 · Booklet p. 9 Q(4a)
items.question: Ahmed bought a book for 18.75 L.E and a pen for 6.30 L.E. Estimate the total cost.
steps: Round purchases: 18.75 L.E rounds to 19 L.E; 6.30 L.E rounds to 6 L.E.
Estimated total: 19 + 6 = 25 L.E. (Actual: 18.75 + 6.30 = 25.05 L.E, diff = 0.05 L.E).

assessmentSheets.title: Booklet Challenge · Adding Decimals
assessmentSheets.tag: Minia British School · Homework Booklet · U1 L7
assessmentSheets.rule: To add three decimals with varying lengths, align every decimal point vertically, pad missing places with zeros, and add from right to left with regrouping.
assessmentSheets.question: From Booklet p. 10, Q(3b) & Q(2a): (1) Find: 12.4 + 6.35 + 0.08. (2) Calculate 14.56 + 9.89.
steps: Step 1: Align vertically and pad 12.4 to 12.40: 12.40 + 6.35 + 0.08.
Step 2: Add hundredths column: 0 + 5 + 8 = 13 hundredths → write 3, carry 1 to tenths.
Step 3: Add tenths column: 1 (carried) + 4 + 3 + 0 = 8 tenths.
Step 4: Add whole numbers: 12 + 6 + 0 = 18 ones → Result = 18.83.
assessmentSheets.note: Pad 12.4 with a zero so it becomes 12.40. Misaligning tenths with hundredths is the most frequent calculation error.

items.label: Question 1 · Booklet p. 10 Q(3b)
items.question: Find: 12.4 + 6.35 + 0.08.
steps: Hundredths: 0 + 5 + 8 = 13 (write 3, carry 1). Tenths: 1 + 4 + 3 + 0 = 8. Ones: 12 + 6 = 18.

items.label: Question 2 · Booklet p. 10 Q(2a)
items.question: Calculate: 14.56 + 9.89.
steps: Align vertically: 14.56 + 9.89.
Hundredths: 6 + 9 = 15 (5, carry 1). Tenths: 1 + 5 + 8 = 14 (4, carry 1). Ones: 1 + 14 + 9 = 24.

assessmentSheets.title: Booklet Challenge · Modeling Subtraction
assessmentSheets.tag: Minia British School · Homework Booklet · U1 L8
assessmentSheets.rule: When subtracting a decimal from a whole number, rewrite the whole number with a decimal point and zeros (12 = 12.00, 1 = 1.000). Regroup across zeros from left to right.
assessmentSheets.question: From Booklet p. 11, Q(3b) & Q(2b): (1) Find: 12 − 5.47. (2) Calculate: 1 − 0.001.
steps: Step 1: Rewrite 12 as 12.00 to match the 2 decimal places of 5.47.
Step 2: Regroup from ones across tenths into hundredths: 12.00 becomes 11 ones, 9 tenths, and 10 hundredths.
Step 3: Subtract: 10 − 7 = 3 (hundredths); 9 − 4 = 5 (tenths); 11 − 5 = 6 (ones) → 6.53.
Step 4: For (2): 1.000 − 0.001: 1 one regrouped gives 9 tenths, 9 hundredths, 10 thousandths. 10 − 1 = 9 → 0.999.
assessmentSheets.note: Check by adding back: 6.53 + 5.47 = 12.00 and 0.999 + 0.001 = 1.000. Inverse addition verifies subtraction instantly.

items.label: Question 1 · Booklet p. 11 Q(3b)
items.question: Find: 12 − 5.47.
steps: Rewrite 12 as 12.00 to match decimal places of 5.47.
Regroup: 12.00 becomes 11 ones, 9 tenths, 10 hundredths.
Subtract: 10 − 7 = 3 (hundredths); 9 − 4 = 5 (tenths); 11 − 5 = 6 (ones) → 6.53.

items.label: Question 2 · Booklet p. 11 Q(2b)
items.question: Calculate: 1 − 0.001.
steps: Rewrite 1 as 1.000 to match thousandths.
Regroup 1 one into 9 tenths, 9 hundredths, 10 thousandths.
Subtract: 10 − 1 = 9 (thousandths); 9 − 0 = 9; 9 − 0 = 9 → 0.999.

assessmentSheets.title: Booklet Challenge · Estimating Differences
assessmentSheets.tag: Minia British School · Homework Booklet · U1 L9
assessmentSheets.rule: To estimate decimal differences, round each number to the nearest whole before subtracting. Compare with the exact difference to verify reasonability.
assessmentSheets.question: From Booklet p. 12, Q(3b) & Q(4a): (1) Estimate then subtract: 24.35 − 11.68. (2) A shopper had 50 L.E and spent 27.65 L.E. Estimate the change and calculate actual.
steps: Step 1: Estimate 24.35 − 11.68: 24.35 rounds to 24; 11.68 rounds to 12. Estimated difference: 24 − 12 = 12.
Step 2: Calculate actual difference: 24.35 − 11.68 = 12.67 (Difference between estimate and actual is only 0.67).
Step 3: Estimate shopper change: 50 − 28 = 22 L.E (rounding 27.65 to 28).
Step 4: Calculate exact change: 50.00 − 27.65 = 22.35 L.E (Estimate 22 L.E is within 0.35 L.E).
assessmentSheets.note: Because 27.65 is closer to 28 than 27, rounding up to 28 gives an estimate of 22, very close to the exact 22.35 L.E.

items.label: Question 1 · Booklet p. 12 Q(3b)
items.question: Estimate then subtract: 24.35 − 11.68.
steps: Round to whole: 24.35 → 24; 11.68 → 12. Estimated difference: 24 − 12 = 12.
Calculate actual difference: 24.35 − 11.68 = 12.67 (Difference = 0.67).

items.label: Question 2 · Booklet p. 12 Q(4a)
items.question: A shopper had 50 L.E and spent 27.65 L.E. Estimate the change and calculate actual.
steps: Estimate: 50 − 28 = 22 L.E (rounding 27.65 to 28).
Actual change: 50.00 − 27.65 = 22.35 L.E (Estimate 22 L.E is within 0.35 L.E).

assessmentSheets.title: Booklet Challenge · Subtracting to Thousandths
assessmentSheets.tag: Minia British School · Homework Booklet · U1 L10
assessmentSheets.rule: Subtracting across three decimal zeros requires cascade regrouping from the whole number through tenths and hundredths into thousandths.
assessmentSheets.question: From Booklet p. 13, Q(3b) & Q(4a): (1) Find: 20 − 13.256. (2) A wire was 4.5 m long. A piece of 1.275 m was cut. How long is the remaining wire?
steps: Step 2: Regroup from 20 ones → leaves 19 ones, 9 tenths, 9 hundredths, and 10 thousandths.
Step 3: Subtract: 10 − 6 = 4 (thous.); 9 − 5 = 4 (hund.); 9 − 2 = 7 (tenths); 19 − 13 = 6 (ones) → 6.744.
assessmentSheets.note: Remember to pad 4.5 m with two zeros to make 4.500 m before subtracting 1.275 m!

items.label: Question 1 · Booklet p. 13 Q(3b)
items.question: Find: 20 − 13.256.
steps: Regroup 20 ones → leaves 19 ones, 9 tenths, 9 hundredths, 10 thousandths.

items.label: Question 2 · Booklet p. 13 Q(4a)
items.question: A wire was 4.5 m long. A piece of 1.275 m was cut. How long is the remaining wire?
steps: Pad to thousandths: 4.500 − 1.275.
Regroup: 4.500 becomes 4.4(9)(10).

assessmentSheets.title: Booklet Challenge · Decimal Story Problems
assessmentSheets.tag: Minia British School · Homework Booklet · U1 L11
assessmentSheets.rule: Multi-step story problems require identifying intermediate totals first (addition) before finding the final unknown (subtraction).
assessmentSheets.question: From Booklet p. 14, Q(4a) & Q(1a): (1) Sara bought a bag for 145.75 L.E and shoes for 89.5 L.E. She paid with 300 L.E. How much change did she receive? (2) If a + 3.45 = 7.2, find a.
steps: Step 1: Step 1 (Total spent): Add bag and shoes: 145.75 + 89.50 = 235.25 L.E.
Step 2: Step 2 (Change received): Subtract total spent from 300 L.E: 300.00 − 235.25.
Step 3: Regroup 300.00: 300 becomes 299 and 100 hundredths. 300.00 − 235.25 = 64.75 L.E.
assessmentSheets.answer: (1) Total spent = 235.25 L.E | Change = 64.75 L.E  |  (2) a = 3.75
assessmentSheets.note: Break word problems into clearly labeled steps: Step 1 = Total purchases, Step 2 = Change. Check: 235.25 + 64.75 = 300.00 L.E.

assessmentSheets.title: Booklet Challenge · Expressions vs Equations
assessmentSheets.tag: Minia British School · Homework Booklet · U2 L1
assessmentSheets.rule: An Expression has no equals sign (e.g. x − 5.23). An Equation equates two expressions with "=" (e.g. x − 5.23 = 9.42). In "subtract A from B", B comes FIRST: B − A.
assessmentSheets.question: From Booklet p. 15, Q(2b) & Q(1): (1) Write an equation: "We subtract 5.23 from a number to get a result of 9.42". (2) Distinguish: Which of m + 6 = 9, 1.2 − m = 0.2, m + 44 is an expression?
steps: Step 1: Analyze English phrasing "subtract 5.23 from a number": Let the unknown number be x. Subtracting 5.23 from x means x is the starting amount (minuend).
Step 2: Formulate the equation: x − 5.23 = 9.42. (Common error: writing 5.23 − x = 9.42 which is incorrect!).
Step 3: For part (2): Look for the presence of an equals sign "=".
Step 4: m + 6 = 9 (equation), 1.2 − m = 0.2 (equation). Only "m + 44" has no equals sign, so it is an algebraic expression.
assessmentSheets.answer: (1) Equation: x − 5.23 = 9.42  |  (2) Expression: m + 44 (Equations: m + 6 = 9, 1.2 − m = 0.2)
assessmentSheets.note: Remember the phrase "subtract from": the number following "from" is always written first in the subtraction expression!

m + 44 has no equals sign, so it is an algebraic expression.

assessmentSheets.title: Booklet Challenge · Variables in Equations
assessmentSheets.tag: Minia British School · Homework Booklet · U2 L2
assessmentSheets.rule: When solving subtraction equations: If variable is minuend (A − b = c), add: A = c + b. If variable is subtrahend (a − z = c), subtract: z = a − c.
assessmentSheets.question: From Booklet p. 16, Q(3a) & Q(3b): Solve for the variable: (1) A − 32.61 = 12.28  |  (2) 3.245 − z = 1.265.
steps: Step 1: Analyze (1) A − 32.61 = 12.28: A is the total (whole). To find the whole, add the parts: A = 12.28 + 32.61.
Step 3: Analyze (2) 3.245 − z = 1.265: 3.245 is the whole; z and 1.265 are the parts. To find the missing part z, subtract: z = 3.245 − 1.265.
assessmentSheets.note: Use a Bar Model to check! In A − 32.61 = 12.28, A sits at the top (whole). In 3.245 − z = 1.265, 3.245 sits at the top, so z = 3.245 − 1.265.

assessmentSheets.title: Booklet Challenge · Stories with Numbers
assessmentSheets.tag: Minia British School · Homework Booklet · U2 L3
assessmentSheets.rule: "less than" reverses word order: "5 less than x" means x − 5 (NOT 5 − x). In age word problems, set up an equation with a variable before solving.
assessmentSheets.question: From Booklet p. 17, Q(2a), Q(3b) & Q(4a): (1) Write expression: "5 less than x". (2) Write & solve: "When 7 is subtracted from a number, the result is 15". (3) Mona is 3 years older than brother. If Mona is 12, how old is her brother?
steps: Step 1: For (1): "5 less than x" translates to x − 5.
Step 2: For (2): Let the number be n. "7 is subtracted from n" gives n − 7. "Result is 15" gives equation: n − 7 = 15. Solve: n = 15 + 7 = 22.
Step 3: For (3): Let brother age be b. Mona is 3 years older → b + 3 = 12 (or 12 − b = 3).
Step 4: Solve for brother age: b = 12 − 3 = 9 years old.
assessmentSheets.answer: (1) x − 5  |  (2) Equation: n − 7 = 15 ⇒ n = 22  |  (3) Equation: b + 3 = 12 ⇒ Brother is 9 years old
assessmentSheets.note: Beware the "less than" trap: 5 less than 10 is 10 − 5 = 5, not 5 − 10. So "5 less than x" is ALWAYS x − 5.

items.label: Question 3 · Booklet p. 17 Q(4a)
items.question: Mona is 3 years older than her brother. If Mona is 12, how old is her brother?
steps: Let brother's age be b. Equation: b + 3 = 12.
Solve: b = 12 − 3 = 9 years old.
